name: Facial masculinization surgery

card.summary: Gender-affirming craniofacial surgery that squares the jaw, projects the chin and builds up the forehead and brow; the literature is mostly reviews and case reports, and looksmaxxers borrow the techniques for appearance goals.
card.aka: FMS, facial confirmation surgery, FFS-style forehead work
card.note: A major surgical category using implants, grafts and osteotomies; published evidence is largely reviews and case series.

quick.overview:
Facial masculinization surgery (FMS) is an umbrella term for procedures that make facial features read as more masculine, chiefly forehead and brow augmentation, jaw and chin augmentation, and Adam's apple enhancement. It is mainly performed as gender-affirming care for trans men and other transmasculine people.

In looksmaxxing circles the same toolkit is discussed for cis men who want a more prominent forehead, brow ridge or jaw. Forum posts ask how to change the forehead shape without work on the bone, and are often redirected in search results to facial feminization procedures such as brow bone shaving.
quick.mechanism: Surgeons add or reshape skeletal and soft tissue: forehead implants, bone grafts, bone cement or fat grafting; jaw angle and chin implants or osteotomies; and cartilage grafts at the thyroid cartilage. Planning often uses CT scans and virtual surgical planning with custom guides and implants.
quick.risks: Complications depend on the procedure and include infection, implant movement or asymmetry, and nerve injury in jaw and chin work. Published evidence for facial masculinization is mostly reviews, case reports and book chapters, and the field has received less research attention than facial feminization.

lead: Facial masculinization surgery (FMS) is a group of reconstructive and aesthetic procedures that make facial features more masculine, mainly performed as gender-affirming surgery for trans men and transmasculine people [1][2]. Procedures include forehead augmentation to create a less rounded forehead and stronger brow ridge, jaw and chin augmentation, and a rib-cartilage procedure to enlarge the Adam's apple first reported in 2017 [1][3].

Surgical planning commonly relies on CT scans compared with a reference skull, with custom cutting guides and implants [4]. Wikipedia notes that FMS is less common than facial feminization surgery and that its literature is mostly case reports, reviews and book chapters [1]. The Wikipedia article describes FMS as rarely medically indicated because testosterone often produces enough change in the facial skeleton, while a 2016 WPATH position statement considers it medically necessary for many trans men [1].

The term also appears in looksmaxxing discussion, where members consider skeletal forehead and jaw work for masculine appearance goals [5]. No studies were found that examine FMS for cisgender appearance enhancement.

Gender-affirming care for trans men; discussed for appearance in forums
CT scans, virtual surgical planning, custom implants and guides [4]

paras: Forehead and brow: According to Wikipedia, the goal is a less rounded forehead with a more prominent supraorbital ridge, using implants, bone grafts, fat grafting, molded bone cement, or outpatient injectable fillers [1]. A 2023 review notes that the upper third of the face strongly influences gender perception and that forehead contouring can involve augmentation or reduction, orbital contouring and hairline adjustment [6]. Injectable fillers have been studied for forehead contouring in a post-marketing study of a hyaluronic acid product [7].

Jaw and chin: Procedures aim for a squarer jaw with a sharper mandibular angle using hydroxyapatite grafts or custom implants, and chin implants or osteotomy to widen and project the chin tip [1][4]. Virtual planning includes forehead augmentation and gonial angle and chin augmentation for FMS [4].
Adam's apple: A newer procedure uses rib cartilage to augment the thyroid cartilage, first described in a 2017 case report [1][8].

sections.h: Differences between male and female faces
paras: A review of sex-related facial characteristics states that sex-based differences appear in nearly every component of the face, from craniofacial structure to soft tissue distribution, and offers a framework for surgical planning [9]. A three-dimensional morphology study applied sex differences in adult faces to gender-affirming surgery [10].

Reviews of gender-affirmation surgery say the data are comparatively sparse and large gaps exist, although these procedures are reported to reduce gender dysphoria and improve well-being in patients [11]. Most research on facial gender-confirming surgery concerns facial feminization, which was pioneered in the 1980s [12]. Outcome data for FMS specifically are limited to case reports and reviews [1][12].

A review of facial gender-affirming surgery pitfalls states that facial surgery requires skill in both craniofacial and aesthetic plastic surgery and that setting realistic expectations is critical [13]. Wikipedia's description of facial feminization surgery lists nerve injury in chin and jaw work, tooth root damage, infection, non-union, and implant shifting or asymmetry among risks of related procedures [14]. A 2023 review of forehead contouring reported that contouring procedures are generally well tolerated despite the proximity of the frontal sinus [6]. Another review examined barriers patients face in finding a gender-affirming surgeon [15].

One looksmax.org thread discusses a forehead that the poster describes as too rounded and wide at the frontal bone, asking how to masculinize it in ways other than bone work, noting that searches steer toward forehead feminization, brow bone shaving or hairline lowering [5]. Skeletal procedures such as genioplasty, jaw implants and brow bone work are broadly grouped as hardmaxxing in these communities.

Human data on FMS consist of reviews, case reports and technique descriptions, including the first reported female-to-male facial confirmation surgery with an Adam's apple procedure [8][12]. A prospective open-label post-marketing study examined a hyaluronic acid filler for forehead contouring [7], and registered trials have tested fillers for forehead contouring [16][17]. No controlled studies were found of skeletal facial masculinization performed for appearance enhancement in cisgender men.

timeline.event: Surgeons Darrell Pratt and Douglas Ousterhout begin the work that leads to modern facial feminization surgery [14].
Ousterhout outlines FMS procedures, building on Paul Tessier's work, according to Wikipedia [1].
WPATH position statement describes FMS as medically necessary for many trans men [1].
First reported female-to-male facial confirmation surgery with a new Adam's apple procedure [8].
Review on anatomy and virtual surgical planning for FFS and FMS is published [4].

lore.intro: FMS terminology is borrowed from gender-affirming care; looksmaxxing posts use it to discuss skeletal forehead and jaw changes [5].

claims.claim: Skeletal forehead and brow work can masculinize the upper face.
claims.believers: A poster describes a rounded forehead and asks how to masculinize it, noting that search results point to feminization procedures [5].
claims.experts: Reviews report that the upper third of the face strongly affects perceived gender and that forehead contouring is performed in both directions with implants, grafts or reduction [6][4].

claims.claim: Jaw and chin implants or fillers are a route to a more masculine lower face.
claims.believers: Community members discuss jaw and chin procedures as part of hardmaxxing plans.
claims.experts: Virtual planning literature lists gonial angle and chin augmentation with custom implants as part of FMS [4]. Wikipedia notes limited research attention and mostly case reports [1].

claims.claim: Non-bony options such as fillers or fat can contour the forehead.
claims.believers: The forum poster explicitly seeks fixes for the forehead outside the bone [5].
claims.experts: A post-marketing study of a hyaluronic acid filler for forehead contouring and a report on fat grafting for forehead contouring in facial feminization exist [7][18].
